BS‑GAT: a network intrusion detection 
system based on graph neural network for edge 
computing
Yalu Wang1   , Zhijie Han2, Ying Du1,3,4*, Jie Li5 and Xin He2 
Abstract 
The emergence of Edge Computing has led to an increasingly intricate and widespread issue of network infiltration 
in Edge Computing devices. Therefore, it is crucial to explore intelligent, automated, and resilient methods for network 
intrusion detection. Graph neural network-based techniques for network intrusion detection have been proposed 
by many scholars recently. However, the graph construction methods of these approaches cannot fully adapt to real 
network intrusion datasets, leading to problems such as overfitting and insufficient graph information mining. Fur-
thermore, the methods employed in the model training phase are relatively limited, failing to consider the character-
istic presence of grouping within networks. These shortcomings result in a lack of high accuracy in intrusion detection 
systems, especially in multi-class classification scenarios. This research suggests a graph neural network technique 
based on behavior similarity employing a graph attention network (BS-GAT) to handle the aforementioned problem. 
To address overfitting and inadequate graph information mining, a behavioral similarity-based graph creation method 
is first presented through an analysis of real datasets. Subsequently, the inclusion of edge behavioral relationship 
weights into the GAT leverages the relationship between data flow and graph structural information, enhancing 
the performance of the trained model. In the final stage, experiments were executed using the most recent datasets 
to assess the effectiveness of the proposed behavior similarity-based graph attention network in network intrusion 
detection. The findings indicate that the proposed approach is highly effective and significantly outperforms existing 
solutions. In binary classification, recall, precision, f1-score, and accuracy all exceed 99%. For multi-class performance, 
the recognition accuracy exceeds 93%, the weighted recall surpasses 91%, and the weighted f1-score exceeds 92%, 
showing a substantial improvement in multi-class recognition effectiveness.
Keywords  Internet of Things, Network intrusion, Graph neural network, Behavior similarity, Graph construction
Introduction
As time progresses, the scale of Internet of Things (IoT) 
devices has grown significantly. They have become 
increasingly intricate, encompassing various functional 
devices such as smart TVs, smartphones, smart speakers, 
smart water purifiers, routers, smart rice cookers, wire-
less smoke detectors, wireless printers, and so on. These 
devices interconnect via edge devices, forming edge 
networks (Ghasempour 2019). Consequently, the num-
ber and frequency of attacks on edge computing device 
networks have grown exponentially. To facilitate the 
advancement of the IoT and ensure the security of smart

networks, researching methods for detecting network 
intrusions on edge computing devices is of paramount

Network intrusion detection (NID) methods can be 
broadly categorized into two types: feature-based and 
machine learning(ML)-based, as outlined in Lo et  al. 
(2022). Feature-based NID systems rely on a prede-
fined set of attack features to analyze and identify sus-
picious patterns within captured data flows. The quality 
of the characteristics utilized is a major determinant of 
this detection method’s efficacy. However, it may not be 
able to respond appropriately to new forms of attacks, 
which could result in poor detection performance. 
Modern NID techniques are based on machine learn-
ing, with the majority utilizing utilize data flow informa-
tion directly for identification, as referenced in (He et al. 
2019; Lawal et al. 2020; Sarhan et al. 2011; Ahmad et al. 
2022; Churcher et al. 2021). While these methods effec-
tively address the feature dependence issue and demon-
strate good detection performance against new attacks, 
their precision in identification falls short for real-world 
network applications. Recently, researchers have shifted 
focus towards the emerging field of ML known as graph 
neural networks (GNNs), introducing several novel NID 
techniques (Lo et al. 2022; Zhou et al. 2021; Chang and 
Paula 2021). GNNs are a specialized type of neural net-
work tailored for graph correlation properties. Over the 
past few years, they have been widely applied across vari-
ous domains, including social networks (Kipf and Welling 
2016), network analysis (Jiang 2021), traffic management 
(Jiang and Jiayun 2022), medical treatment (Zhang et al. 
2021a), and distributed computing (Sun et  al. 2021). 
Given that networks are fundamentally graph-based sys-
tems, integrating GNNs into NID techniques is a logi-
cal progression that is expected to significantly enhance 
detection accuracy.
NID methods leveraging GNNs typically involve two 
primary steps: graph construction and model training. 
Graph construction entails utilizing available network 
data and establishing connections to create a logically 
coherent graph representation. Model training refers to 
utilizing neural networks on the generated graph to train 
models used for identifying edges or nodes. The detec-
tion performance of NID techniques based on GNNs 
is better than that of conventional machine learning-
based techniques. However, both graph creation and 
model training provide practical challenges for current 
NID techniques based on GNNs. For instance, the logic 
behind graph construction is singular, failing to consider 
the characteristics of network data flow, which could lead 
to insufficient graph information mining (Lo et al. 2022; 
Chang and Paula 2021). Furthermore, the direct applica-
tion of existing model training techniques neglects the 
interdependencies among grouped nodes (Zhou et  al. 
2021). Consequently, this oversight leads to reduced 
accuracy in NID methods based on GNNs, particularly in 
multi-classification scenarios.
To address the aforementioned issues, this paper pro-
poses a Graph Attention Network(GAT) algorithm 
based on behavioral similarity (BS-GAT) which is used 
to improve model training as well as graph creation. In 
the graph construction phase, behavioral rules are repre-
sented as edges, and data flow as nodes, This creating a 
network in which each node has a consistent number of 
neighbors. This technique effectively addresses overfit-
ting and imperfect graph information mining problems. 
Weights based on behavioral similarity are introduced in 
the model training phase to address the node grouping 
characteristics. By employing these methods and con-
ducting experiments on the latest flow-based datasets, 
the results show binary classification accuracy exceeding 
98% and multi-classification accuracy surpassing 93%, 
effectively addressing the issue of low accuracy in multi-
class scenarios.
To summarize, this paper makes three primary 
contributions:
•	 We introduce a distinctive GAT based on behavioral 
similarity to address the NID problem. By leverag-
ing behavioral similarity, a novel method for graph 
creation is devised. Data flows are regarded as nodes 
within the graph, while the behavior rules of these 
nodes serve as edges, creating of a graph where each 
node has a relatively uniform number of neighbors. 
This approach effectively addresses issues like uneven 
graph construction and overfitting prevalent in other 
GNN-based NID methods.
•	 We incorporate the weighted edge behavior relation-
ships into the GAT, enabling the aggregation of fea-
tures from hidden layer nodes. This enhancement 
allows NID methods to better leverage the relation-
ships between data flows and the structural informa-
tion within the graph.
•	 Through experiments using the most recent net-
work flow information, the suggested NID strategy is 
assessed. The experimental results demonstrate that 
the proposed method performs better as compared 
to standard NID methods and graph neural network-
based NID techniques.
The remainder of the paper is structured as fol-
lows: Sect.  "Related work" presents an overview of the 
advancements made by scholars in the domain of NID 
methods. Sect. "Behavior similarity based GAT for NID" 
initially provides an introduction to GNN and GAT, fol-
lowed by a detailed exposition of the proposed method.

Related work
Numerous researchers have developed machine learn-
ing-based techniques for detecting network intrusions 
in recent years. From traditional machine learning tech-
niques to the advent of graph-based techniques and ulti-
mately to graph neural network-based techniques, these 
algorithms have developed over time.
Used a unique hierarchical progressive network struc-
ture, He et al. (2019) proposed a multi-modal sequence 
NID method by extracting different feature levels from 
network connections, leveraging LSTM and Multi-Modal 
Deep Autoencoder (MDAE) techniques. In Ahmad 
et  al. (2022), the authors compare various techniques 
for developing NID systems and select the optimal fea-
tures from the dataset based on the correlation between 
features. Building upon this, they propose an AdaBoost-
based NID method and provide a detailed description 
of its functionality and performance. These approaches 
train directly on the dataset without taking into account 
the graph topology information. As a result, each train-
ing data point remains relatively isolated, unable to fully 
exploit the information contained within the dataset. 
Consequently, these methods exhibit limited efficacy 
in detecting intricate network attacks, such as Botnet 
attacks (Vormayr et  al. 2017; Bhuyan et  al. 2011; Kam-
bourakis et al. 2007), which require a more comprehen-
sive network perspective and traffic analysis. Therefore, 
seeking a method that can encompass a global network 
view and traffic for improving the performance of intru-
sion detection is of significant importance, such as 
enhancing generalization and stability.
Qingsai et al. (2020) combined statistical features with 
latent features, transforming network traffic into first-
order and second-order graphs. The first-order graph 
learns latent features from the perspective of individual 
nodes, while the second-order graph learns latent fea-
tures from a global perspective. Then, classifier methods 
were applied to anomaly detection, yielding favorable 
results on two real datasets. In Islam et  al. (2020),the 
authors proposed a four-stage intrusion detection sys-
tem that uses the chi-squared method and can detect 
both strong and weak cyber attacks in a CAN. This work 
is the first-ever graph-based defense system proposed 
for the CAN. Despite the fact that both of these tech-
niques employ graph-based techniques to solve intrusion

Due to the remarkable performance of GNN on graph-

tion method for Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based 
intrusion detection in budget-constrained IoT systems, 
achieving a hierarchy-aware black-box adversarial attack 
strategy. Lo et  al. (2022) proposed the E-GraphSAGE 
architecture, a variant of GraphSAGE tailored for cap-
turing both edge features and topology information 
in graphs for NID within the IoT. Chang et  al. (2021) 
enhanced the E-GraphSAGE architecture by introducing 
the E-ResGAT architecture based on Graph Attention 
Networks (GAT). The primary innovation lies in integrat-
ing residual learning into GNN by exploiting available 
graph information. The three methods, despite utilizing 
GNNs, suffer from overfitting during graph construction, 
highly uneven neighbor counts, insufficient graph infor-
mation extraction, and neglect of node grouping. These 
issues result in post-aggregation nodes with blurred fea-
tures and isolated points, leading to lower accuracy in 
multi-class classification.
It is clear from the aforementioned publication that 
many researchers struggle to achieve high identification 
accuracy in NID, especially in multi-class classification.

GNN and GAT​
The goal of this research is to create a model that can help 
edge servers identify network threats using the GAT as 
the training network. In recent years, GNN has emerged 
as one of the fastest-developing subfields of deep learning. 
Its ability to learn from graphs allows it to extract informa-
tion that would otherwise remain hidden. Moreover, GNN 
possesses the adaptability to generalize to dynamic changes 
in network topology, rendering it particularly suitable for 
non-spectral graph-structured data. With the advance-
ment of GNN, several derivatives have emerged, including 
GAT (Veličković et al. 2017), GCN (Kipf and Welling 2016), 
GraphSAGE (Hamilton et al. 2017), among others, which 
have garnered widespread attention from scholars. Nota-
bly, GAT stands out as a GNN that integrates attention 
mechanisms. This enables automatic computation of atten-
tion coefficients between nodes and subsequent aggrega-
tion of information from neighboring nodes based on these 
coefficients. Consequently, mining graphical data is more

BS based graph construction
Training a GNN model mainly consists of two steps. 
First, constructing a graph input for the GNN by struc-
turing the dataset into a graph based on reasonable rules. 
Then, using the structure of the GNN to train the graph 
generated in the previous step and produce a model.
As shown in Fig. 4a, we aim to construct a graph where 
the number of neighbors for each node is relatively bal-
anced. Having too many or too few neighbors can be 
detrimental to using GNNs for model training. When 
the number of neighbors is too large, it can cause the fea-
tures to become blurred, leading to incorrect recognition 
results. A node may turn into an isolated point or edge 
if it does not have adequate number of neighbors. For 
example, the isolated edge I shown in the dashed ellipse

IoT devices establish connections through networks, 
where the data traffic exchanged between these devices 
essentially represents their behavioral data. In this con-
text, IoT devices can be viewed as entities similar to 
individuals, with network flow data analogous to human 
behavior. The process of identifying network flows is 
comparable to profiling individuals in social networks. 
This paper adopts a grouping approach based on the dis-
tinctive features of human behavior to categorize net-
work traffic. This approach aids in constructing a graph 
with relatively uniform neighbor counts.
Because humans exhibit social attributes, their collec-
tive behavior possesses three characteristics:
(1)	 An individual’s multiple behaviors exhibit self-simi-
larity.
(2)	 The behaviors among different individuals within 
the same group exhibit some similarities.
(3)	 The behaviors of individuals from different groups 
exhibit significant differences.
These characteristics can be correlated with the actions 
of IoT nodes. Data flows are considered to represent the 
actions of a single node if their source IP addresses are 
the same. They are categorized as representing the behav-
ior of the same type of node if the subnet masks are same.

BS based GAT​
According to the GAT algorithm, all attention coef-
ficients which are comparable to the similarity values 
between a node and its neighboring nodes are automat-

captured when neighboring nodes are aggregated using 
automatically learnt attention coefficients.

behavioral similarities. When aggregating features 
from the hidden layers of nodes, the process should be

Due to the large volumes of data in the BoT-v2 and 
ToN-v2 datasets, with 37,763,497 and 16,940,496 
instances respectively, training on the entire dataset 
would be highly time-consuming. Therefore, this paper 
adopts a partial data approach for experimentation. 
Each experiment selects data that encompasses all cat-
egories in the dataset and is repeated multiple times. 
The average of all results from these repetitions is then 
taken as the final result. Additionally, the dataset used 
for each experiment is divided into three parts: 50% of 
the dataset is utilized for training, 20% for validation, 
and the remaining 30% for testing the model’s accuracy. 
This approach not only increases efficiency but also 
demonstrates the stability of the proposed algorithm.
Experimental setting
(A)	
Evaluation Metrics
This paper’s experiment is segmented into two sec-
tions: assessing node neighbor uniformity and evaluat-
ing classification accuracy. Consequently, the experiment 
will discuss evaluation metrics specific to each of these 
sections.
(1)	Average degree of the number of neighbors of a node
This paper utilizes the Gini coefficient (Dorfman 1979) 
to assess the average degree of a node’s neighbors. Equa-
tion (7) and Fig. 6 below outline the calculation method 
and schematic diagram, respectively. The Gini coeffi-
cient primarily measures the income inequality among 
residents, with values ranging from 0 to 1. A higher Gini 
coefficient indicates greater income disparity, while a 
lower value suggests less disparity and more uniform 
income distribution among all residents. In this paper, 
the Gini coefficient is used to represent the disparity in 
the number of neighbors a node acquires after graph 
generation. A higher Gini coefficient indicates a more 
uneven distribution of neighbors among node, whereas 
a lower value indicates a more even distribution. The 
application of the Gini coefficient in network intrusion 
detection is also quite extensive (Li et  al. 2018; Disha 
and Waheed 2022; Zhang et al. 2021b). Interested read-
ers can refer to the provided literature for more detailed 
information.
(2)	Classification accuracy
To assess the identification accuracy of the NID 
method proposed in this paper, the evaluation metrics 
from Table 5 are employed to compare it with previously 
proposed algorithms (KNN, SVM, Random Forest, Extra 
Trees, E-GraphSAG, E-ResGAT, GAT), Extra Trees is 
the classification method used by the dataset provider. 
The baseline methods compared in this paper have been 
extensively cited in these literature (Chang and Paula 
2021; Khan et  al. 2023; Aljuhani et  al. 2022; Ma et  al. 
2023; Altaf et  al. 2023; Shuaiyi et  al. 2023) on network 
intrusion detection and are frequently used as bench-
marks for comparison. In addition, these metrics are con-
sidered crucial and classical in the field of classification 
recognition, widely utilized across numerous articles.

To further analyze the effectiveness of the proposed

on two datasets, as shown in Fig. 9, are provided. It can

samples. This demonstrates that the proposed method 
has very low FPR and FNR in data stream detection.
FPR and FNR are crucial for network intrusion detec-
tion. A false negative means identifying an attack flow as 
benign, while a false positive means identifying a benign 
flow as an attack. If these two metrics are high, it is very 
detrimental to network intrusion detection. Therefore, 
this paper compares the FPR and FNR across different 
methods, as shown in Table 8. The results indicate that 
the proposed method has lower FPR and FNR than other 
methods.
Since only a portion of the dataset was used for each 
experiment, Table  9 displays the average results of 
various metrics for seven methods in binary classifica-
tion. Among them, both E-GraphSAG and E-ResGAT 
exhibit recall rates exceeding 96% on the two datasets, 
consistent with their reported results. However, the 
algorithm proposed in this paper still outperforms the 
other six algorithms on both datasets. Additionally, 
the proposed algorithm demonstrates excellent perfor-
mance in precision as well. On the ToN-v2 dataset, its 
performance is only 0.33% lower than E-ResGAT but 
surpasses GAT and E-GraphSAG by 10.46% and 3.24%, 
respectively. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm out-
performs the other six algorithms in F1-Score, indicat-
ing its robustness.

Conclusions
To address the issue of NID, this paper proposes an 
advanced graph neural network-based method that intro-
duces the concept of behavior similarity as the logical 
rule for graph construction and as a training constraint 
for the GNN. The core approach involves grouping 
data flows as nodes in the graph, constructing edges 
based on behavior rules, and incorporating the behavior 
weight matrix into the training of the GAT. This method 
addresses issues such as uneven neighbor distribution 
among nodes, insufficient information mining, and over-
fitting in GNNs. The final experimental results show that 
the proposed method effectively improves classification 
accuracy, particularly in multi-class classification.
Despite a significant improvement in the precision of 
multi-class classification, the recognition performance 
for certain attacks in multi-class scenarios remains 
unsatisfactory, such as Dos in the ToN-v2 dataset. A 
possible cause of this problem is insufficient integrity 
of the data set. In fact, an important aspect of iden-
tifying a network stream data is to obtain the state of 
the sender of the stream data. For example, during 
Dos attacks, the network parameters of the sender will 
be very active. Therefore, in the future it will be nec-
essary to improve the existing dataset and study it to 
make it develop better solutions to multi-classification 
problems.

Abstract: The emergence of Edge Computing has led to an increasingly intricate and widespread issue of network infiltration in Edge Computing devices. Therefore, it is crucial to explore intelligent, automated, and resilient methods for network intrusion detection. Graph neural network-based techniques for network intrusion detection have been proposed by many scholars recently. However, the graph construction methods of these approaches cannot fully adapt to real network intrusion datasets, leading to problems such as overfitting and insufficient graph information mining. Fur- thermore, the methods employed in the model training phase are relatively limited, failing to consider the character- istic presence of grouping within networks. These shortcomings result in a lack of high accuracy in intrusion detection systems, especially in multi-class classification scenarios. This research suggests a graph neural network technique based on behavior similarity employing a graph attention network (BS-GAT) to handle the aforementioned problem. To address overfitting and inadequate graph information mining, a behavioral similarity-based graph creation method is first presented through an analysis of real datasets. Subsequently, the inclusion of edge behavioral relationship weights into the GAT leverages the relationship between data flow and graph structural information, enhancing the performance of the trained model. In the final stage, experiments were executed using the most recent datasets to assess the effectiveness of the proposed behavior similarity-based graph attention network in network intrusion detection. The findings indicate that the proposed approach is highly effective and significantly outperforms existing solutions. In binary classification, recall, precision, f1-score, and accuracy all exceed 99%. For multi-class performance, the recognition accuracy exceeds 93%, the weighted recall surpasses 91%, and the weighted f1-score exceeds 92%, showing a substantial improvement in multi-class recognition effectiveness.
